stem: Who is credited with performing the first human cardiac catheterization in 1929 by inserting a catheter into his own vein?
explanation: As a urology registrar, he successfully advanced a catheter through his own cubital fossa vein into the right atrium and documented it with an X-ray.
rationale: He was a urology registrar who used his own body to prove the procedure's feasibility.

optionExplanations.A: As a urology registrar, he successfully advanced a catheter through his own cubital fossa vein into the right atrium and documented it with an X-ray.
optionExplanations.B: While a pioneer in the field, he is known as the father of interventional cardiology for his work in the 1960s, long after the first catheterization.
optionExplanations.C: He was involved in the later development of the field in the 1940s and 1950s, focusing on systematic hemodynamic measurements.
optionExplanations.D: He worked alongside Cournand to evolve catheterization into a diagnostic tool for studying pulmonary circulation later in the 20th century.

source.hint: He was a urology registrar who used his own body to prove the procedure's feasibility.
